abstractions: Two sign-in attempts and owners, five wrong-code attempts and three ack attempts.
Opaque PKCE states, proofs and credentials are represented by identities. Cryptography, endpoint shapes and encrypted persistence are checked by existing implementation tests.

Storage failure before the key commit ends the attempt. After key persistence, cancellation cannot stop acknowledgement. Authentication delivery precedes best-effort Steward logout and local-session cleanup.

Failed durable callback burn and cancellation retain pending bytes. A process restart cannot resume browser authorization without a fresh live attempt. A recovered key acknowledgement loses the transient previous-token revocation capability. Acknowledged receipts may remain after refused cleanup and are retried through normal restart recovery.

Legacy top-level key/receipt/ack fields describe the current Attempt. The canonical activation record retains an older committed owner during replacement admission. CurrentActivationProjection requires matching representations when both refer to the same committed attempt. beginWork represents the queued worker reaching the replacement pending write after old cleanup. Restart preserves durable replacement pending bytes while restoring the stored activation owner.
Durable browser records retain their own identity across failed cancellation and later email/phone admission. Current-owner callback exclusion does not claim that unrelated older records were erased.

The optional reserve/persistDispatch/reserveFailed transitions split confirmation admission from its awaited local CAS. confirm remains the existing post-commit macro. committing retains the prior saved review and has not issued a provider request.

Current versus retained byte caps are scaled to two and three units, with four representing preflight overflow.

Rollback restores only its captured provider revision. A newer provider revision makes it fail without overwriting it.

A same-generation rebind preserves runtime admission and avoids shutdown. Committed writes and later reported outcomes are separate transitions; provider removal updates presence for subsequent operations.

abstractions: Two logical account/grant identities, two draft identities and content/attachment equivalence classes. Each retained operation instance issues at most one provider request in a trace.

Current capability readback gates confirmation. Capability callbacks retain account, binding epoch and read token. Grant withdrawal during an already admitted run is deferred, so an in-flight request can remain uncertain and its receipt is retained.

Cleanup requires a provider-confirmed current send. Edited copies are preserved and an older saved version is marked. The compatibility cleanup action summarizes a complete pass; per-write actions expose retained, shelf and saved CAS completion, lost replies and stale-binding compensation.

The staged cleanup projection admits one cleanup invocation at a time. Its shelf represents one exact source draft. Arbitrary shelf collections and simultaneous independent cleanup invocations require further schedules.
Three immutable one-shot operation histories represent create, replacement and provider deletion. Local copies remain independent of provider deletion.
Forwarded originals are source-part IDs and a history/byte equivalence class. Provider metadata is captured at review; non-atomic replacement may overwrite later provider changes.
One lifecycle owner and one replacement owner, finite content/ref identities. Controlled external provider ports do not establish installed Gmail behavior.
One local adoption transaction is pending at a time. Private fields and imported-map members not directly observed remain explicit bounded-refinement gaps.
